STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate, rectangular/square white plate with a rim band and flat centre, no inner wall visible. Food sits flat on the surface.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plate, appears roughly 20-25 cm across; a medium dinner-size square plate, so about 24 cm.
b) Reference: the plate's width spans roughly 3 bacon strips laid end to end... more practically, the sausage slices (about 3 cm diameter) sit along the upper right edge with room for about 7 slices across the plate width, giving roughly 7 x 3.3 cm ≈ 23 cm.
Both cues agree: width ≈ 24 cm, so area ≈ 24² = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items (footprint and thickness):
- Bacon: about 4-5 strips, covering roughly 12% of the plate (~70 cm²), flat layer about 0.4 cm thick. Volume ≈ 28 cm³, density ~1.0, but cooked bacon is light; estimate ~30 g.
- Pork sausage/chorizo slices: 6 round slices, each ~3 cm diameter, ~0.8 cm thick, ~11 cm² total footprint × 0.8 ≈ 9 cm³ per... total ≈ 6 slices × 7 cm³ ≈ 40 cm³ → ~40 g.
- Pineapple chunks: about 8 cubes ~2.5 cm each, roughly 80 cm² footprint, one cube layer 2 cm thick averaging ~1.2 cm; volume ≈ 80 × 1.2 ≈ 95 cm³ × 0.6 ≈ 60 g.
- Roasted potato cubes: about 8 cubes ~2 cm, footprint ~60 cm², average thickness ~1.5 cm → 90 cm³; density 0.8 for cooked starch → ~70 g.
- Brussels sprouts: about 9 halved/whole sprouts, ~2.5 cm each, footprint ~50 cm², thickness ~1.5 cm → 75 cm³ × 0.6 ≈ 45 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer under toppings; the plate is a single flat layer, so no hidden food beyond the items above.

STEP 5 - Energy per 100 g (cooked, as served):
- Bacon, cooked: ~540 kcal/100 g
- Cooked pork sausage: ~300 kcal/100 g
- Pineapple: ~50 kcal/100 g
- Roasted potato: ~130 kcal/100 g (with light oil, around 150)
- Brussels sprouts, cooked with oil: ~60 kcal/100 g

Total weight ≈ 245 g; energy ≈ 162 + 120 + 30 + 105 + 27 ≈ 445 kcal.
